To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

delayed cerebral necroses, after radiation of the brain, can be divided into hemispereal and midline lesions; that the midline lesions, which are caused by radiation, can be divided in two groups: those of the brainstem (pons) and those of the cerebral hemi-spheres (thalamus and basal ganglia); and that the midline necroses are to be differentiated from the delayed hemispheric lesions by their symptoms, their course and prognosis, as well

the tolerance dose for the cerebral midline structures, as a function of the dose rate, is 50 Gy for 2 weeks and 60 Gy for 4 weeks, and that the tolerance dose is not dependent on the volume of the midline structure irradiated, but is related to the total volume of the brain.

delayed radiation necroses of the midline are to be differentiated from hemispheric necroses, as their latency is much shorter (2-6 weeks), their course much more severe, and their prognosis much less favorable.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of hemispheric necroses, a dose of 60 Gy in the course of 6 weeks is tolerated, whereas midline necroses occur at a much lower dose of 40 Gy.
the cerebral midline structures, especially the corpus callosum and the fornix, are more susceptible to delayed radiation damage than the cerebral hemispheral structures.
, in the region of the cerebral midlines, the tolerance limit of radiation is much lower than the one in the hemispheres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the midline structures are more sensitive to irradiation than the hemispheric structures, and that a dose of 4000 rads is the limit for the former and of 6000 rads for the latter.
the midline structures of the brain are more radiosensitive, but not more radiation-tolerant, than the cerebral hemispherics.
, with the help from the NSD-concepts, a dose of 5000 NSD for the hemispheric brain structures and a dose of 3000 NSD for cerebral midline structures can be tolerated without any risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation necroses in the cerebral hemispheric tissue are not to be considered as a contraindication for further radiotherapic procedures.
the midline is the most sensitive area in the brain to radiation necrosis.
radiation tolerance of midline structures is limited.
